data.long_meaning: Heetka is derived from the Sanskrit word 'heet', meaning 'sun'. It is a name that embodies the warmth and radiance of the sun, symbolizing strength, beauty, and grace. The name Heetka carries the meaning “Sun” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Heetka usually hope their child will grow to embody sun and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Heetka is a name that is deeply rooted in Hindu spirituality. It is believed to invoke the blessings of the Sun God, who is a source of energy, light, and life. The name is also associated with the goddess Helia, who is the goddess of the sun and the embodiment of vitality and creativity.
data.etymology: Heetka belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Sun.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Heetka total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

historical_references.reference:
Heetka was a legendary king of the Vatsa dynasty, ruling around 4th century BC in the ancient Indian kingdom of Magadha.
Context: Heetka is mentioned in Jain texts, particularly in the works of Acharya Hemachandra, as a powerful ruler who was sympathetic towards Jainism and provided many concessions and patronage to the Jain community.

Heetka, also known as Heetaka II, was a king of the Satavahana dynasty, ruling around 1st century AD in the Deccan region of ancient India.
Context: Heetka is known for issuing the Edicts of Heetaka, which were inscriptions that set out laws, regulations, and taxes. The inscriptions also reveal that Heetka was a patron of Buddhism and that he took an active role in maintaining peace and order within his realm.
